summary: Reproduced both counterexamples from https://github.com/amdpilot-org/sglang/pull/2335 against candidate https://github.com/amdpilot-org/sglang/pull/2280 at 4b0d2276a4cf6ce3e6ed5d2c7f66dce81416d0ac. Preserved the candidate's tracked-snapshot cast and corrected the following GDN prefill boundary by running causal convolution on active cache slots in activation dtype, then restoring updated slots to the configured cache dtype.

tests.what_was_measured: On gfx950, FP16 activation/BF16 cache and BF16/BF16 succeeded; BF16 activation/FP32 cache and BF16 activation/FP16 cache failed in ROCm Triton compilation with mismatched new_conv_state branch types. See candidate_before.txt.
All four dtype combinations compiled and ran on gfx950. Output and final cache values matched an independent grouped torch.nn.functional.conv1d reference; see corrected_after.txt.
18 tests, 27 subtests passed, including selected-slot dtype conversion/writeback and the candidate's snapshot-store cases; see pytest_policy.txt.
Existing causal-convolution branch-state GPU regression passed (1 passed, 245 deselected).

gpu_evidence: AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950 with ROCm 7.2 executed the failing candidate compiler cases and passing corrected numerical cases; raw output is retained in candidate_before.txt and corrected_after.txt.
remaining_limitations: QuantTrio/Qwen3.6-27B-AWQ weights were unavailable, so full serving and semantic accuracy were not tested.
The available GPU was AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950 with ROCm 7.2, not the reporter's NVIDIA RTX 5090 SM120 with CUDA 13.3.
The tiny Llama fixture cannot qualify the qwen3_5 hybrid-GDN architecture and was not substituted as proof.
No native source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
